passages.text: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
passages.sermon: We reached the shore safely.\r\nWe learned the name of the island.\r\nThe island was called Malta.
passages.original: Καὶ διασωθέντες τότε ἐπέγνωμεν ὅτι Μελίτη ἡ νῆσος καλεῖται

passages.text: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
passages.sermon:
The people who lived on the island met us.
They were not Jews or Greeks.
They showed us great kindness.
They did not act with ordinary friendliness.
They started a fire for us.
They welcomed every one of us.
They did this because it was raining.
They did this because it was cold.
passages.original: οἵ τε βάρβαροι παρεῖχον οὐ τὴν τυχοῦσαν φιλανθρωπίαν ἡμῖν ἅψαντες γὰρ πυρὰν προσελάβοντο πάντας ἡμᾶς διὰ τὸν ὑετὸν τὸν ἐφεστῶτα καὶ διὰ τὸ ψῦχος

passages.text: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian apostle.
Paul gathered a bundle of sticks.
He laid the sticks on the fire.
The heat drove a viper out from the sticks.
The viper fastened itself to Paul's hand.
passages.original: Συστρέψαντος δὲ τοῦ Παύλου φρυγάνων τι πλῆθος καὶ ἐπιθέντος ἐπὶ τὴν πυράν ἔχιδνα ἀπὸ τῆς θέρμης ἐξελθοῦσα καθῆψεν τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
passages.sermon:
The islanders saw the creature hanging from Paul's hand.
They spoke to each other.
They said, "This man is surely a murderer."
Paul survived the sea.
Justice has not allowed him to live.
passages.original: ὡς δὲ εἶδον οἱ βάρβαροι κρεμάμενον τὸ θηρίον ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἔλεγον Πάντως φονεύς ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος ὃν διασωθέντα ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης ἡ Δίκη ζῆν οὐκ εἴασεν

passages.text: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
passages.sermon: Paul was bitten by a viper.\r\nHe shook the viper off into the fire.\r\nHe did not suffer any harm.
passages.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν ἀποτινάξας τὸ θηρίον εἰς τὸ πῦρ ἔπαθεν οὐδὲν κακόν

passages.text: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
passages.sermon:
The islanders watched Paul.
They expected Paul to swell up.
They also expected Paul to fall down dead suddenly.
They waited a long time.
They saw nothing unusual happen to Paul.
They changed their minds.
They said Paul was a god.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ προσεδόκων αὐτὸν μέλλειν πίμπρασθαι ἢ καταπίπτειν ἄφνω νεκρόν ἐπὶ πολὺ δὲ αὐτῶν προσδοκώντων καὶ θεωρούντων μηδὲν ἄτοπον εἰς αὐτὸν γινόμενον μεταβαλόμενοι ἔλεγον αὐτὸν εἶναι θεόν

passages.text: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
passages.sermon:
Publius was the chief official of the island.
He owned an estate near that place.
Publius welcomed us.
He showed us kindness.
He entertained us for three days.
He was hospitable.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ τοῖς περὶ τὸν τόπον ἐκεῖνον ὑπῆρχεν χωρία τῷ πρώτῳ τῆς νήσου ὀνόματι Ποπλίῳ ὃς ἀναδεξάμενος ἡμᾶς ἡμέρας τρεῖς φιλοφρόνως ἐξένισεν

passages.text: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.
passages.sermon:
Publius was the chief official of the island.
His father was very sick.
He lay in bed.
He suffered from fever.
He also had dysentery.
Paul went in to see him.
Paul prayed for him.
Paul placed his hands on him.
Paul healed him.
passages.original: ἐγένετο δὲ τὸν πατέρα τοῦ Ποπλίου πυρετοῖς καὶ δυσεντερίῳ συνεχόμενον κατακεῖσθαι πρὸς ὃν ὁ Παῦλος εἰσελθὼν καὶ προσευξάμενος ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ ἰάσατο αὐτόν

passages.text: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian apostle.
Paul healed the father of Publius.
After this, other sick people on the island came.
These people also had illnesses.
They came to Paul.
Paul healed them too.
passages.original: τούτου δὲ γενομένου καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ οἱ ἐν τῇ νήσῳ ἔχοντες ἀσθενείας προσήρχοντο καὶ ἐθεραπεύοντο

passages.text: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.
passages.sermon: The islanders lived on the island where Paul healed the sick.\r\nThey honored us in many ways.\r\nThey gave us what we needed when we were ready to sail.
passages.original: οἳ καὶ πολλαῖς τιμαῖς ἐτίμησαν ἡμᾶς καὶ ἀναγομένοις ἐπέθεντο τὰ πρὸς τὰς χρείας

passages.text: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions stayed on the island for three months.
After three months, they set sail.
They traveled in an Alexandrian ship.
The ship had spent the winter on the island.
The ship had the Twin Brothers as its figurehead.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ τρεῖς μῆνας ἀνήχθημεν ἐν πλοίῳ παρακεχειμακότι ἐν τῇ νήσῳ Ἀλεξανδρινῷ παρασήμῳ Διοσκούροις

passages.text: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
passages.sermon: Paul and his companions arrived at Syracuse.\r\nThey stopped their journey there.\r\nThey stayed in Syracuse for three days.
passages.original: καὶ καταχθέντες εἰς Συρακούσας ἐπεμείναμεν ἡμέρας τρεῖς

passages.text: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.
passages.sermon:
Paul was traveling to Rome as a prisoner.
He was with other people on a ship.
They left Syracuse.
They set sail from there.
They came to Rhegium.
One day passed.
A south wind began to blow.
On the second day, they arrived at Puteoli.
passages.original: ὅθεν περιελόντες κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Ῥήγιον καὶ μετὰ μίαν ἡμέραν ἐπιγενομένου νότου δευτεραῖοι ἤλθομεν εἰς Ποτιόλους

passages.text: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.
passages.sermon:
We arrived at Puteoli.
We found some Christian brothers there.
They invited us to stay with them for seven days.
After that, we traveled to Rome.
passages.original: οὗ εὑρόντες ἀδελφοὺς παρεκλήθημεν παρ’ αὐτοῖς ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας ἑπτά καὶ οὕτως εἰς τὴν Ῥώμην ἤλθαμεν

passages.text: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.
passages.sermon:
The Christian brothers in that place heard news about us.
They traveled to meet us.
They came as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns.
Paul saw these brothers.
Paul gave thanks to God.
Paul felt encouraged.
passages.original: Κἀκεῖθεν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἀκούσαντες τὰ περὶ ἡμῶν ἦλθαν εἰς ἀπάντησιν ἡμῖν ἄχρι Ἀππίου Φόρου καὶ Τριῶν Ταβερνῶν οὓς ἰδὼν ὁ Παῦλος εὐχαριστήσας τῷ Θεῷ ἔλαβε θάρσος

passages.text: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle and a prisoner.
We arrived in Rome.
The authorities allowed Paul to live by himself.
A soldier guarded Paul.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ εἰσήλθομεν εἰς Ῥώμην ἐπετράπη τῷ Παύλῳ μένειν καθ’ ἑαυτὸν σὺν τῷ φυλάσσοντι αὐτὸν στρατιώτῃ

passages.text: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul arrived in Rome as a prisoner.
After three days, Paul called together the leaders of the Jews in Rome.
The leaders of the Jews gathered to meet Paul.
Paul spoke to them.
Paul said, “Brothers, I have done nothing against our people.
I have done nothing against the customs of our fathers.
Even so, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem.
They handed me over to the Romans.”
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς συνκαλέσασθαι αὐτὸν τοὺς ὄντας τῶν Ἰουδαίων πρώτους συνελθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἔλεγεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐγώ ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί οὐδὲν ἐναντίον ποιήσας τῷ λαῷ ἢ τοῖς ἔθεσι τοῖς πατρῴοις δέσμιος ἐξ Ἱεροσολύμων παρεδόθην εἰς τὰς χεῖρας τῶν Ῥωμαίων

passages.text: They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.
passages.sermon: The Romans examined me.\r\nThey wanted to release me.\r\nThey found no reason for a death sentence against me.
passages.original: οἵτινες ἀνακρίναντές με ἐβούλοντο ἀπολῦσαι διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν αἰτίαν θανάτου ὑπάρχειν ἐν ἐμοί

passages.text: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.
passages.sermon:
The Jews objected to my release.
They did not agree with the decision.
Because of their objection, I was forced to appeal to Caesar.
I did not appeal because I had any accusation against my own nation.
I have no charge to bring against my people.
passages.original: ἀντιλεγόντων δὲ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἠναγκάσθην ἐπικαλέσασθαι Καίσαρα οὐχ ὡς τοῦ ἔθνους μου ἔχων τι κατηγορεῖν

passages.text: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner in Rome.
Paul called the Jewish leaders to meet him.
Paul wanted to see them and speak with them.
Paul wore a chain as a prisoner.
Paul was bound because of the hope of Israel.
passages.original: διὰ ταύτην οὖν τὴν αἰτίαν παρεκάλεσα ὑμᾶς ἰδεῖν καὶ προσλαλῆσαι ἕνεκεν γὰρ τῆς ἐλπίδος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ τὴν ἅλυσιν ταύτην περίκειμαι

passages.text: The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.
passages.sermon:
The Jewish leaders spoke to Paul.
They said they had not received any letters about Paul from Judea.
They said none of the brothers from Judea had come and reported anything bad about Paul.
They said no one from Judea had spoken anything evil about Paul.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπαν Ἡμεῖς οὔτε γράμματα περὶ σοῦ ἐδεξάμεθα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας οὔτε παραγενόμενός τις τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἀπήγγειλεν ἢ ἐλάλησέν τι περὶ σοῦ πονηρόν

passages.text: But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”
passages.sermon:
The Jewish leaders spoke to Paul.
They said, “We want to hear what you believe.
People everywhere speak against this group.
We know this sect is opposed in all places.
We think your opinion is important.
We want to listen to you.”
passages.original: ἀξιοῦμεν δὲ παρὰ σοῦ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ φρονεῖς περὶ μὲν γὰρ τῆς αἱρέσεως ταύτης γνωστὸν ἡμῖν ἐστιν ὅτι πανταχοῦ ἀντιλέγεται

passages.text: So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
The leaders set a day to meet with Paul.
Many people came to the place where Paul was staying.
Paul spoke to them from morning until evening.
He explained the kingdom of God to them.
He testified about the kingdom of God.
He tried to persuade them about Jesus.
He used the Law of Moses and the Prophets to explain about Jesus.
passages.original: Ταξάμενοι δὲ αὐτῷ ἡμέραν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν ξενίαν πλείονες οἷς ἐξετίθετο διαμαρτυρόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ πείθων τε αὐτοὺς περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπό τε τοῦ νόμου Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν ἀπὸ πρωῒ ἕως ἑσπέρας

passages.text: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the people.
Some people believed what Paul said.
Other people did not believe Paul.
Some accepted his message.
Others refused to accept it.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐπείθοντο τοῖς λεγομένοις οἱ δὲ ἠπίστουν

passages.text: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet: ‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul spoke to a group of people about Jesus.
The people disagreed with each other.
Some people believed Paul.
Other people did not believe Paul.
The people began to leave.
Paul made a final statement before they left.
Paul said the Holy Spirit spoke through Isaiah the prophet.
The Holy Spirit spoke to the ancestors of these people.
The Holy Spirit said, “Go to this people and say this:
‘You will hear with your ears, but you will not understand.
You will see with your eyes, but you will not perceive.’”
passages.original: ἀσύμφωνοι δὲ ὄντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἀπελύοντο εἰπόντος τοῦ Παύλου ῥῆμα ἓν ὅτι Καλῶς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐλάλησεν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ὑμῶν λέγων Πορεύθητι πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον καὶ εἰπόν Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε

passages.text: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’
passages.sermon:
This people have a callous heart.
They do not feel or care in their hearts.
They hardly hear with their ears.
They do not listen well.
They have closed their eyes.
They do not want to see.
If they saw with their eyes, they would notice the truth.
If they heard with their ears, they would understand the message.
If they understood with their hearts, they would turn back to God.
If they turned back, I would heal them.
passages.original: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν μή‿ ποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς

passages.text: Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the Jewish leaders in Rome.
Paul said, “You must know this.
God has sent His salvation to the Gentiles.
The Gentiles will listen.”
passages.original: Γνωστὸν οὖν ἔστω ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπεστάλη τοῦτο τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ αὐτοὶ καὶ ἀκούσονται

passages.text: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul lived in his own rented house.
Paul stayed there for two full years.
Paul welcomed everyone who came to visit him.
passages.original: Ἐνέμεινεν δὲ διετίαν ὅλην ἐν ἰδίῳ μισθώματι καὶ ἀπεδέχετο πάντας τοὺς εἰσπορευομένους πρὸς αὐτόν

passages.text: Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul lived in his own rented house in Rome.
Paul spoke with boldness.
Paul spoke without hindrance.
Paul proclaimed the kingdom of God.
Paul taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ διδάσκων τὰ περὶ τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ πάσης παρρησίας ἀκωλύτως
